docs.title: rl-sandbox
docs.text:
rl-sandbox is a toolbox for implementing, training, evaluating, and comparing reinforcement learning algorithms against registered Gymnasium environments.

The project provides reusable boundaries for trainers, action policies, environments, checkpoints, episode execution, metrics, replay, and visualisation. REINFORCE is the first implemented training algorithm, while CartPole-v1 and Acrobot-v1 are the initial environments used to exercise the toolbox.

docs.title: Current capabilities
docs.text:
• Train REINFORCE policies on registered discrete-action environments.
  • Run random or trained policies through a shared episode runner.
  • Evaluate training with reward, loss, entropy, and deterministic evaluation metrics.
  • Save self-describing, algorithm-aware checkpoints.
  • Capture episode frames and replay them independently of a live environment.
  • Extend the trainer and policy abstractions to evaluate additional algorithms.

class BaseEnvApp(ABC):
    """Abstract env wrapper.

    Owns the gym.Env, an asyncio.Lock for concurrent access, and tracks the
    current observation across steps. Concrete subclasses (e.g., GymEnvApp)
    must set `spec`, `env`, `lock`, and `current_obs` as instance attributes
    in `__init__`, and implement `apply_action` and `reset_env`.
    """

    spec: EnvSpec
    env: gym.Env
    lock: asyncio.Lock
    current_obs: np.ndarray

    @abstractmethod
    def apply_action(self, action_policy: BaseActionPolicy) -> StepResult: ...

    @abstractmethod
    def reset_env(self) -> None: ...

docs.title: Gymnasium implementation
docs.text:
GymEnvApp — concrete BaseEnvApp backed by a Gymnasium environment.

Construction takes an EnvSpec; gym.make is called using spec.env_id, so the same class works for any registered environment.

Physics timing

Each gym env advances by a fixed timestep (spec.physics_tick_s) per env.step() call. The wall-clock delay between steps controls how fast the simulation appears to run, not how the physics behaves.

class GymEnvApp(BaseEnvApp):
    """Generic gym-env wrapper parameterised by an EnvSpec."""

    def __init__(self, spec: EnvSpec) -> None:
        self.spec: EnvSpec = spec
        self.env: gym.Env = gym.make(spec.env_id, render_mode="rgb_array")
        self.env.action_space.seed(ACTION_SPACE_SEED)
        self.lock: asyncio.Lock = asyncio.Lock()
        obs, _info = self.env.reset()
        self.current_obs: np.ndarray = obs
        logger.info(f"Created GymEnvApp({spec.env_id}). Initial observation: {obs}")
        logger.info(
            f"Action space: {self.env.action_space}, "
            f"Observation space: {self.env.observation_space}"
        )

    def apply_action(self, action_policy: BaseActionPolicy) -> StepResult:
        """Take an action using the current observation, advance env, return result."""
        action: int = action_policy.choose_action(
            self.env.action_space, self.current_obs
        )
        obs, reward, terminated, truncated, _info = self.env.step(action)
        self.current_obs = obs
        done: bool = terminated or truncated
        if done:
            logger.info(
                f"Received reward {reward} and observation {obs}. "
                f"Episode ended by {'termination' if terminated else 'truncation'}."
            )
        return StepResult(
            obs=obs,
            reward=float(reward),
            terminated=bool(terminated),
            truncated=bool(truncated),
            done=done,
        )

    def reset_env(self) -> None:
        """Reset the environment."""
        obs, _info = self.env.reset()
        self.current_obs = obs
        logger.info(f"Environment reset. Initial observation: {obs}")

class EpisodeRunner:
    """Runs episodes against a BaseEnvApp.

    Does not store policy or config — receives them per-call for clarity.
    All run methods are async and acquire app.lock around env access.
    """

    def __init__(self, app: BaseEnvApp) -> None:
        self._app = app
        self._current_episode: int = 0
        self._total_steps: int = 0
        self._episode_steps: int = 0

    @property
    def current_episode(self) -> int:
        return self._current_episode

    def increment_episode(self) -> None:
        self._current_episode += 1

    @property
    def total_steps(self) -> int:
        return self._total_steps

    def increment_total_steps(self) -> None:
        self._total_steps += 1

    @property
    def episode_steps(self) -> int:
        return self._episode_steps

    def increment_episode_steps(self) -> None:
        self._episode_steps += 1

    def reset_episode_steps(self) -> None:
        self._episode_steps = 0

    def on_step_transition(self) -> None:
        self.increment_episode_steps()
        self.increment_total_steps()

    def _check_max_steps_reached(self, config: EpisodeConfig) -> bool:
        if config.max_steps is not None and self._episode_steps >= config.max_steps:
            logger.info(
                f"Episode {self._current_episode} hit max_steps ({config.max_steps})."
            )
            return True
        return False

    async def run_episode(
        self,
        policy: BaseActionPolicy,
        config: EpisodeConfig,
        capture_frames: bool = False,
    ) -> tuple[EpisodeResult, list[np.ndarray] | None]:
        """Run a single episode, stepping env under the lock until done or max_steps.

        When capture_frames is True, grabs env.render() under the same lock as
        env.step() at each step and returns the list of RGB frames. Otherwise
        returns None for the frames component.
        """
        sequence: list[StepResult] = []
        frames: list[np.ndarray] = [] if capture_frames else []
        self.reset_episode_steps()

        async with self._app.lock:
            self._app.reset_env()

        episode_done: bool = False
        while not episode_done:
            async with self._app.lock:
                step_result = self._app.apply_action(policy)
                if capture_frames:
                    frame: np.ndarray = self._app.env.render()  # type: ignore[assignment]
                    frames.append(frame)

            self.on_step_transition()
            sequence.append(step_result)
            if step_result.done:
                logger.info(
                    f"Episode {self._current_episode} ended after {self._episode_steps} steps."
                )
            episode_done = self._check_max_steps_reached(config) or step_result.done

            tick = self._app.spec.physics_tick_s / config.sim_speed_multiplier
            await asyncio.sleep(tick)

        self.increment_episode()
        result = EpisodeResult(
            sequence=sequence,
            timestamp=datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc),
            policy_name=type(policy).__name__,
            episode_config=config,
            timesteps_reached=len(sequence),
        )
        return result, frames if capture_frames else None

    async def run_batch(
        self, policy: BaseActionPolicy, config: BatchConfig
    ) -> tuple[BatchResult, dict[int, list[np.ndarray]]]:
        """Run a batch of episodes sequentially.

        Returns the BatchResult and a dict mapping episode index to captured
        frames for episodes selected by config.replay_freq.
        """
        episodes: list[EpisodeResult] = []
        captured_frames: dict[int, list[np.ndarray]] = {}
        for i in range(config.no_episodes):
            should_capture = i % config.replay_freq == 0
            result, frames = await self.run_episode(
                policy, config.episode_config, capture_frames=should_capture
            )
            episodes.append(result)
            if frames is not None:
                captured_frames[i] = frames
        return BatchResult(episodes=episodes, batch_config=config), captured_frames

class FileOps:
    """Handles persistence of batch recording data (frames + metadata)."""

    @staticmethod
    def save(
        captured_frames: dict[int, list[np.ndarray]],
        metadata: BatchRecording,
        path: Path,
    ) -> None:
        """Save captured episode frames and metadata to disk.

        Writes frames.npz (numpy arrays) and metadata.json to the given directory.
        """
        path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        sorted_keys: list[int] = sorted(captured_frames.keys())
        arrays: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {
            REPLAY_EPISODES_KEY: np.array(sorted_keys),
        }
        for pos, ep_idx in enumerate(sorted_keys):
            arrays[f"{FRAMES_KEY_PREFIX}{pos}"] = np.array(captured_frames[ep_idx])

        np.savez(path / FRAMES_FILE_NAME, **arrays)

        with open(path / METADATA_FILE_NAME, "w") as f:
            json.dump(metadata.model_dump(), f, indent=2, default=str)

    @staticmethod
    def load_batch_replay(path: Path) -> BatchReplay:
        """Load frames + metadata from disk and return a BatchReplay."""

        with open(path / METADATA_FILE_NAME) as f:
            recording: BatchRecording = BatchRecording(**json.load(f))

        data: np.lib.npyio.NpzFile = np.load(path / FRAMES_FILE_NAME)
        replay_episodes: np.ndarray = data[REPLAY_EPISODES_KEY]

        replay_lookup: dict[int, int] = {
            int(ep_idx): pos for pos, ep_idx in enumerate(replay_episodes)
        }

        episodes: list[EpisodeReplay] = []
        for ep_rec in recording.episodes:
            if ep_rec.episode_index in replay_lookup:
                pos: int = replay_lookup[ep_rec.episode_index]
                frame_array: np.ndarray = data[f"{FRAMES_KEY_PREFIX}{pos}"]
                frames: list[np.ndarray] = [
                    frame_array[i] for i in range(frame_array.shape[0])
                ]
            else:
                frames = []
            episodes.append(EpisodeReplay(frames=frames, metadata=ep_rec))

        return BatchReplay(
            episodes=episodes,
            source_path=str(path),
            total_source_episodes=recording.no_episodes,
            replay_freq=recording.replay_freq,
            env_spec=recording.env_spec,
        )

class ColourFormatter(logging.Formatter):
    """Custom formatter that adds ANSI colour codes to log output."""

    RESET: str = "\033[0m"
    CYAN: str = "\033[36m"
    MAGENTA: str = "\033[35m"

    LEVEL_COLOURS: dict[int, str] = {
        logging.DEBUG: "\033[37m",  # white
        logging.INFO: "\033[32m",  # green
        logging.WARNING: "\033[33m",  # yellow
        logging.ERROR: "\033[31m",  # red
        logging.CRITICAL: "\033[1;31m",  # bold red
    }

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__(
            fmt="%(asctime)s %(levelname)-8s %(name)s %(message)s",
            datefmt="%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S",
        )

    def format(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> str:
        level_colour: str = self.LEVEL_COLOURS.get(record.levelno, self.RESET)

        record.asctime = (
            f"{self.CYAN}{self.formatTime(record, self.datefmt)}{self.RESET}"
        )
        padded_level: str = f"{record.levelname:<8}"
        record.levelname = f"{level_colour}{padded_level}{self.RESET}"
        record.name = f"{self.MAGENTA}{record.name}:{record.lineno}{self.RESET}"

        return f"{record.asctime} {record.levelname}{record.name} {record.getMessage()}"

class LoggerFactory:
    """Factory for configuring the root logger."""

    @staticmethod
    def setup(config: LoggingConfig | None = None) -> None:
        if config is None:
            config = LoggingConfig()

        root_logger: logging.Logger = logging.getLogger()
        root_logger.setLevel(logging.DEBUG)

        # Console handler
        console_handler: logging.StreamHandler = logging.StreamHandler(sys.stderr)
        console_handler.setLevel(getattr(logging, config.log_level.upper()))
        console_handler.setFormatter(ColourFormatter())
        root_logger.addHandler(console_handler)

        # File handler
        log_file: Path = Path(config.log_file_path)
        log_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        file_handler: logging.FileHandler = logging.FileHandler(str(log_file))
        file_handler.setLevel(logging.DEBUG)
        file_handler.setFormatter(
            logging.Formatter(
                fmt="%(asctime)s %(levelname)-8s %(name)s %(message)s",
                datefmt="%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S",
            )
        )
        root_logger.addHandler(file_handler)

class ReinforcePolicy(BaseActionPolicy):
    """Policy that uses a trained PolicyNetwork to select actions.

    Forward-passes the actual current observation through the network and
    samples from the resulting categorical distribution.
    """

    def __init__(self, network: PolicyNetwork) -> None:
        self._network: PolicyNetwork = network

    def choose_action(self, action_space: spaces.Space, observation: np.ndarray) -> int:
        """Sample an action from the policy network's output distribution."""
        obs_tensor: torch.Tensor = torch.tensor(
            observation, dtype=torch.float32
        ).unsqueeze(0)
        with torch.no_grad():
            probs: torch.Tensor = self._network(obs_tensor)
        dist: torch.distributions.Categorical = torch.distributions.Categorical(probs)
        return int(dist.sample().item())

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path: Path, expected_env_id: str) -> "ReinforcePolicy":
        """Load a trained policy from disk; raise if algorithm or env_id mismatch."""
        raw: dict = torch.load(path, weights_only=True)
        checkpoint: Checkpoint = Checkpoint.model_validate(raw)
        if checkpoint.algorithm != ALGORITHM_REINFORCE:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Checkpoint algorithm {checkpoint.algorithm!r} "
                f"is not a REINFORCE checkpoint (expected {ALGORITHM_REINFORCE!r})"
            )
        if checkpoint.env_id != expected_env_id:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Checkpoint env_id {checkpoint.env_id!r} "
                f"does not match expected env {expected_env_id!r}"
            )
        network: PolicyNetwork = PolicyNetwork(
            obs_size=checkpoint.obs_size,
            action_size=checkpoint.action_size,
            hidden_size=checkpoint.hidden_size,
        )
        network.load_state_dict(checkpoint.state_dict)
        network.eval()
        return cls(network=network)

class MatplotlibAnimator(BaseRenderer):
    """Renderer that uses Matplotlib to render frames."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._fig: Figure | None = None
        self._ax: Axes | None = None
        self._img: Any | None = None
        self._quit_requested: bool = False

    def quit(self) -> None:
        """Signal the live rendering loop to quit."""
        self._quit_requested = True

    def _ensure_fig(self) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
        """Return the existing (fig, ax) or create a new one."""
        if self._fig is None or self._ax is None:
            self._fig, self._ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 5))
            self._ax.axis("off")
        return self._fig, self._ax

    def init_display(self) -> None:
        """Initialise the display window (non-blocking). Idempotent."""
        self._ensure_fig()
        plt.show(block=False)

    def display_frame(self, frame: np.ndarray) -> None:
        """Update display with a single frame and pump the event loop."""
        fig, _ = self._ensure_fig()
        self.update_frame(frame)
        fig.canvas.draw_idle()
        fig.canvas.flush_events()

    def update_frame(self, frame: np.ndarray) -> list[Any]:
        """Update the animation with a new frame."""
        _, ax = self._ensure_fig()
        if self._img is None:
            self._img = ax.imshow(frame)
        else:
            self._img.set_data(frame)
        return [self._img]

    def render_from_frames(self, frames: list[np.ndarray]) -> None:
        """Render an animation from a list of frames."""
        fig, _ax = self._ensure_fig()
        _ani = animation.FuncAnimation(
            fig,
            self.update_frame,
            frames=frames,
            interval=50,
            blit=True,
        )
        plt.show()

    async def start_live_render(
        self, update_frame_callback: Callable[[int], list[Any]]
    ) -> None:
        """Render frames continuously using FuncAnimation."""
        fig, _ax = self._ensure_fig()
        _ani = animation.FuncAnimation(
            fig,
            update_frame_callback,
            frames=None,
            interval=RENDER_DELAY_MS,
            blit=True,
            cache_frame_data=False,
        )
        plt.show(block=False)

        while not self._quit_requested:
            fig.canvas.draw_idle()
            fig.canvas.flush_events()
            await asyncio.sleep(RENDER_DELAY_MS / 1000)
        logger.info("Quit requested. Stopping live render.")

class ReplayRunner:
    """Plays back recorded episode frames via a renderer.

    No dependency on a live env, gymnasium, or asyncio.Lock — replay is
    pure frame playback. The physics tick comes from the EnvSpec embedded
    in the recording.
    """

    def __init__(self, renderer: BaseRenderer) -> None:
        self._renderer = renderer

    async def replay_episode(
        self, episode: EpisodeReplay, physics_tick_s: float
    ) -> None:
        """Play back all frames for a single episode at its recorded speed."""
        meta: EpisodeRecording = episode.metadata
        tick: float = physics_tick_s / meta.sim_speed_multiplier

        logger.info(
            f"Replaying episode {meta.episode_index} "
            f"({meta.timesteps_reached} steps, {meta.sim_speed_multiplier:.1f}x speed)"
        )

        self._renderer.init_display()
        for frame in episode.frames:
            self._renderer.display_frame(frame)
            await asyncio.sleep(tick)

        logger.info(f"Episode {meta.episode_index} complete.")

    async def replay_batch(self, batch: BatchReplay) -> None:
        """Play back all episodes in a batch sequentially."""
        physics_tick_s: float = batch.env_spec.physics_tick_s
        logger.info(
            f"Replaying {len(batch.episodes)} of {batch.total_source_episodes} episodes "
            f"(replay_freq={batch.replay_freq}, env={batch.env_spec.env_id}) "
            f"from {batch.source_path}"
        )
        for episode in batch.episodes:
            await self.replay_episode(episode, physics_tick_s)
        logger.info("Batch replay complete.")

class ReinforceTrainer(BaseTrainer):
    """Trains a policy network using the REINFORCE algorithm.

    At each episode:
    1. Run the policy, collecting (log_prob, reward, entropy) at each step
    2. Compute discounted returns G_t for each step
    3. Normalise returns for variance reduction
    4. Loss = -sum(log_prob * normalised_return)
    5. Backprop and update

    Periodically runs deterministic (argmax) evaluation passes to give a
    cleaner learning signal than the noisy training rewards.

    Env-specific parameters (solved threshold, rolling window) come from
    the EnvSpec — same trainer works on any discrete-action gym env.
    """

    def __init__(self, env: gym.Env, config: TrainingConfig, spec: EnvSpec) -> None:
        super().__init__(env, config)
        self._spec: EnvSpec = spec
        obs_size: int = int(np.prod(env.observation_space.shape))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        action_size: int = int(env.action_space.n)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        self._obs_size: int = obs_size
        self._action_size: int = action_size
        self._network: PolicyNetwork = PolicyNetwork(
            obs_size=obs_size,
            action_size=action_size,
            hidden_size=config.hidden_size,
        )
        self._optimizer: optim.Adam = optim.Adam(
            self._network.parameters(), lr=config.learning_rate
        )

    def train(self) -> TrainingResult:
        """Run the REINFORCE training loop for num_episodes episodes."""
        all_metrics: list[EpisodeMetrics] = []
        evaluations: list[EvalResult] = []
        reward_history: list[float] = []

        for episode_idx in range(self._config.num_episodes):
            metrics: EpisodeMetrics = self._run_episode(episode_idx)
            all_metrics.append(metrics)
            reward_history.append(metrics.total_reward)

            rolling_avg: float = np.mean(
                reward_history[-self._spec.rolling_window :]
            ).item()
            if episode_idx % LOG_INTERVAL_EPISODES == 0:
                logger.info(
                    f"Episode {episode_idx}: reward={metrics.total_reward:.1f}, "
                    f"avg={rolling_avg:.1f}, loss={metrics.loss:.4f}, "
                    f"entropy={metrics.entropy:.3f}"
                )

            episodes_completed: int = episode_idx + 1
            if episodes_completed % EVAL_INTERVAL_EPISODES == 0:
                eval_result: EvalResult = self._evaluate(episode_idx)
                evaluations.append(eval_result)
                logger.info(
                    f"Eval @ ep {episodes_completed}: "
                    f"{eval_result.mean_reward:.1f} ± {eval_result.std_reward:.1f} "
                    f"(over {eval_result.n_episodes} deterministic episodes)"
                )

        final_eval: EvalResult = self._evaluate(self._config.num_episodes - 1)
        evaluations.append(final_eval)
        logger.info(
            f"Final eval: {final_eval.mean_reward:.1f} ± {final_eval.std_reward:.1f} "
            f"(over {final_eval.n_episodes} deterministic episodes)"
        )

        final_avg: float = np.mean(reward_history[-self._spec.rolling_window :]).item()
        return TrainingResult(
            episodes=all_metrics,
            config=self._config,
            env_spec=self._spec,
            final_avg_reward=final_avg,
            solved=final_avg >= self._spec.solved_reward_threshold,
            evaluations=evaluations,
        )

    def _run_episode(self, episode_idx: int) -> EpisodeMetrics:
        """Run one episode, collect log_probs and rewards, then update."""
        log_probs: list[torch.Tensor] = []
        rewards: list[float] = []
        entropies: list[float] = []

        obs, _info = self._env.reset()
        done: bool = False

        while not done:
            obs_tensor: torch.Tensor = torch.tensor(obs, dtype=torch.float32).unsqueeze(
                0
            )
            probs: torch.Tensor = self._network(obs_tensor)
            dist: torch.distributions.Categorical = torch.distributions.Categorical(
                probs
            )
            action: torch.Tensor = dist.sample()
            log_prob: torch.Tensor = dist.log_prob(action)
            entropies.append(dist.entropy().item())

            obs, reward, terminated, truncated, _info = self._env.step(action.item())
            done = terminated or truncated

            log_probs.append(log_prob)
            rewards.append(float(reward))

        returns: list[float] = self.compute_returns(rewards, self._config.gamma)
        returns_tensor: torch.Tensor = torch.tensor(returns, dtype=torch.float32)
        if len(returns_tensor) > 1:
            returns_tensor = (returns_tensor - returns_tensor.mean()) / (
                returns_tensor.std() + 1e-8
            )

        loss: torch.Tensor = torch.zeros(1)
        for log_prob, g in zip(log_probs, returns_tensor):
            loss = loss - log_prob * g

        self._optimizer.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        self._optimizer.step()

        mean_entropy: float = float(np.mean(entropies)) if entropies else 0.0
        return EpisodeMetrics(
            episode=episode_idx,
            total_reward=sum(rewards),
            steps=len(rewards),
            loss=loss.item(),
            entropy=mean_entropy,
        )

    def _evaluate(self, episode_idx: int) -> EvalResult:
        """Run deterministic (argmax) eval episodes with frozen weights."""
        self._network.eval()
        rewards: list[float] = []
        try:
            for _ in range(EVAL_EPISODE_COUNT):
                obs, _info = self._env.reset()
                done: bool = False
                total_reward: float = 0.0
                while not done:
                    obs_tensor: torch.Tensor = torch.tensor(
                        obs, dtype=torch.float32
                    ).unsqueeze(0)
                    with torch.no_grad():
                        probs: torch.Tensor = self._network(obs_tensor)
                    action: int = int(probs.argmax(dim=-1).item())
                    obs, reward, terminated, truncated, _info = self._env.step(action)
                    done = terminated or truncated
                    total_reward += float(reward)
                rewards.append(total_reward)
        finally:
            self._network.train()
        return EvalResult(
            episode=episode_idx,
            mean_reward=float(np.mean(rewards)),
            std_reward=float(np.std(rewards)),
            n_episodes=EVAL_EPISODE_COUNT,
        )

    @staticmethod
    def compute_returns(rewards: list[float], gamma: float) -> list[float]:
        """Compute discounted returns G_t for each timestep.

        G_t = r_{t+1} + gamma * G_{t+1}, computed backwards for efficiency.
        """
        returns: list[float] = []
        g: float = 0.0
        for r in reversed(rewards):
            g = r + gamma * g
            returns.insert(0, g)
        return returns

    def save_model(self, path: Path) -> None:
        """Save weights + algorithm + env identity in a self-describing checkpoint."""
        checkpoint: Checkpoint = Checkpoint(
            state_dict=dict(self._network.state_dict()),
            algorithm=ALGORITHM_REINFORCE,
            env_id=self._spec.env_id,
            obs_size=self._obs_size,
            action_size=self._action_size,
            hidden_size=self._config.hidden_size,
        )
        torch.save(checkpoint.model_dump(), path)

    def load_model(self, path: Path) -> None:
        """Load policy network weights from a self-describing checkpoint."""
        raw: dict = torch.load(path, weights_only=True)
        checkpoint: Checkpoint = Checkpoint.model_validate(raw)
        if checkpoint.algorithm != ALGORITHM_REINFORCE:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Checkpoint algorithm {checkpoint.algorithm!r} "
                f"does not match trainer algorithm {ALGORITHM_REINFORCE!r}"
            )
        if checkpoint.env_id != self._spec.env_id:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Checkpoint env_id {checkpoint.env_id!r} "
                f"does not match trainer env {self._spec.env_id!r}"
            )
        self._network.load_state_dict(checkpoint.state_dict)

class PolicyNetwork(nn.Module):
    """Policy network for REINFORCE.

    Takes an observation and outputs a probability distribution over actions
    via softmax. Two hidden layers with ReLU activations.
    """

    def __init__(self, obs_size: int, action_size: int, hidden_size: int = 128) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.network: nn.Sequential = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(obs_size, hidden_size),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_size, hidden_size),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_size, action_size),
            nn.Softmax(dim=-1),
        )

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return self.network(x)

Self-describing checkpoint schema for a discrete-action policy network.

Captures everything needed to reconstruct a trained policy
  • algorithm: which training algorithm produced the weights (so a loader can refuse a file written by a different algorithm).
  • env_id: which gym env the weights are valid for.
  • obs_size, action_size, hidden_size: architecture sizing the loader needs to rebuild PolicyNetwork before applying state_dict.

Algorithm names are free-form strings rather than a Literal-constrained enum — the schema deliberately makes no commitment to a closed set, so adding a new algorithm doesn't require editing this module. Canonical algorithm names are defined here (e.g. ALGORITHM_REINFORCE) so writer and reader import the same string and typos surface at import time.

On disk the payload is a plain dict (via model_dump()) of allowlisted types (Tensor, str, int, dict), so torch.load(..., weights_only=True) loads it safely. The Pydantic class lives only in-process.

class EnvViewer:
    """Visualises a Gymnasium env by rendering its rgb_array frames."""

    def __init__(self, env: gymnasium.Env, lock: asyncio.Lock | None = None) -> None:
        self.env: gymnasium.Env = env
        self._quit_requested: bool = False
        self.lock: asyncio.Lock = lock or asyncio.Lock()
        self.plotter: BasePlotter = MatplotlibPlotter()
        self.renderer: BaseRenderer = MatplotlibAnimator()
        self.config: ViewerConfig = ViewerConfig()
        self._latest_frame: Any = self.env.render()

    def quit(self) -> None:
        """Signal the live rendering loop to quit."""
        self._quit_requested = True
        self.renderer.quit()

    def plot(self) -> None:
        """Render a single frame from the env."""
        frame = self.env.render()
        self.plotter.plot(frame)  # type: ignore[arg-type]

    def simulate_and_render_sequence(
        self,
        sequence_length: int = 100,
        action_policy: BaseActionPolicy | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        if action_policy is None:
            action_policy = RandomActionPolicy()
        frames: list[Any] = []
        for _ in range(sequence_length):
            frame: Any = self.env.render()
            frames.append(frame)

        self.renderer.render_from_frames(frames)  # type: ignore[arg-type]

    async def render_live(self) -> None:
        async def refresh_frame() -> None:
            """Periodically snapshot the env frame under the lock."""
            while not self._quit_requested:
                async with self.lock:
                    self._latest_frame = self.env.render()
                await asyncio.sleep(0.02)  # ~50 fps
            logger.info("Quit requested. Stopping refresh frame task.")

        def update_frame(frame_num: int) -> list[Any]:
            """FuncAnimation callback — reads the latest cached frame."""
            return self.renderer.update_frame(self._latest_frame)  # type: ignore[arg-type]

        asyncio.ensure_future(refresh_frame())
        await self.renderer.start_live_render(update_frame)
